- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 76.67 → 77.50 in Example 2).
- Model underreacts to sharp downward trends in history (e.g., 78.57 → 76.23 in Example 3, forecast drops only slightly).
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reversion suggests.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent low prices (e.g., 65.80 → 66.49 in Example 3, model still forecasts 70+).
- Model exhibits “overconfidence” in short-term momentum — forecasts often remain high even when true prices are trending down.
- In cases of strong downward momentum, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly enough (e.g., 70.78 → 65.81 in Example 4).
- Forecasts are often too optimistic in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, especially when true prices are declining.
